cita: Kwon and Bang (2026). What Spatial Memory Must Store: Occlusion as the Test for Language-Agent Memory.
problema: Language-agent 'memory palace' systems anchor memories to world coordinates on the intuition that geometry adds retrieval power text cannot, but that intuition is rarely tested: it is unclear whether spatial anchoring should reweight ranking, or instead gate a separate geometric predicate such as visibility/occlusion that flat text or vector retrieval structurally cannot compute.
mecanismo: An agent captures observations while moving through a shared voxel world, writing memories anchored to a 3D subject cell; five representations are compared (text-only cosine null, coordinate-distance recall, a field-of-view cone, and cone-plus-line-of-sight via a ray-versus-voxel DDA re-pointed from the agent's own gaze-ray primitive), isolating whether geometry should be folded into a ranking blend (spatial-as-ranker) or used to select-then-verify a geometric predicate (spatial-as-index/verification), with occlusion as the irreducible test case.
evaluacion: A pre-registered recall experiment (ranker-blend vs. geometry-led weighting vs. position-blind baseline, Wilcoxon test); controlled voxel-simulation pilots on near-duplicate localization and occlusion (McNemar tests, n up to 1144 targets); and a git-committed live pre-registration on the running text-agent relay (SPMEM-OCC-LIVE-v1, 8 worlds, 96 behind-wall targets, pooled exact McNemar).
numeros_clave: Shipped linear blend fails its own frozen test (mean deltaHit@5 -0.0375, Wilcoxon p=0.306, CI includes 0) while geometry-led weighting wins (+0.3208, p<1e-15); near-duplicate localization 1.000 (coordinate recall) vs 0.533 (text null), McNemar p<1e-6; occlusion: text/FoV-cone 0.000 vs cone+DDA 0.982 on 849 behind-wall targets (McNemar p<1e-6); live confirmation false-visible 1.000->0.000, pooled exact McNemar p=2.5e-29; return-and-resume action task: world-bound 1.000 vs flattened 0.611 (p=0.016).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper reports a measured negative result about its own default mechanism: the shipped spatial-proximity-in-a-linear-blend ranker ties or loses to a position-blind baseline (mean deltaHit@5 -0.0375, p=0.306, §6.8) — a documented case of a plausible-sounding feature that does not help, reported honestly rather than hidden.

The central methodological move is refusing to assume geometry helps and instead measuring ranker-form vs index/verification-form separately (§3, §6.8) — direct support for MF's insistence that retrieval mechanisms be measured, not assumed, before being adopted.

The return-and-resume task shows world-bound memory correctly preserves a 'prior-progress note' enabling an agent to resume unfinished work (1.000) while flattened memory discards it and restarts from scratch (0.611, p=0.016, §6.7) — a concrete instance of binding progress/plan-state to a persistent anchor rather than flat text, relevant to MF's plan-state-as-memory axis even though the paper's domain (3D spatial anchoring) is not MF's.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: domain is embodied 3D spatial/occlusion memory in a voxel game world (Space Zero), quite orthogonal to Meta-Factory's software-factory memory use case; digested per protocol because plan_estado=SI and the ranker-vs-index/measured-negative-result methodology (§3, §6.8, p.5-6) does transfer, but direct applicability is genuinely doubtful.

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education.
problema: Multi-round reflection lets an LLM agent recover from failures within a single task, but each task remains an isolated episode: lessons paid for in tokens across many reflection rounds on one task (e.g. a wrong formula, a bad transition timing) are discarded before the next task begins, forcing the agent to re-derive the same class of mistake every time.
mecanismo: A vision-language model scores rendered keyframes of a Manim animation on multiple pedagogical axes; the score both drives an in-task visual-reflection repair loop and gates writes to a dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank: a positive channel M+ stores success rationales (score>=85) as soft Reference Examples, a negative channel M- stores validated failure->success transitions (crash->success, or a >=5-point score improvement) as hard Known Pitfalls; both are LLM-distilled (not literal diffs) and retrieved per-polarity by task embedding on future tasks.
evaluacion: Fixed-probe evaluation (frozen EMB snapshots at K in {0,50,100,200} tested read-only on disjoint probe tasks) against no-memory, matched-budget Manim-code RAG, and shuffled Random-EMB baselines, with blind human Pass@1/quality scoring plus reflection-round counts as headline metrics (VLM scores kept as auxiliary diagnostics only to avoid evaluator leakage), and a channel/gating ablation (Table 1).
numeros_clave: EMB@0->EMB@200: Human Pass@1 62.0->84.9%, quality 3.26->3.88, reflection rounds 12.2->6.5; beats Manim-code RAG (83.3%/3.65/11.4) on all three headline metrics at K=200; ablation 'No M-' (drop negative channel) drops Pass@1 to 75.0 (Table 1, p.8); write gates theta_high=85, delta_fail>=5, k+=2/k-=3.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The negative channel M- stores validated failure patterns as hard 'Known Pitfalls' gated by causal attribution (crash->success or scored improvement >=5, §3.3), and removing it measurably costs Pass@1 (Table 1, p.8) — direct empirical support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge memory.

Both channels are distilled by a dedicated LLM agent at consolidation time rather than storing literal before/after diffs, specifically to strip scene-specific tokens that would mislead retrieval (§3.3 'Lessons are LLM-distilled, not literal diffs') — a concrete gated-distillation recipe MF could adopt when promoting gotchas to durable recipes.

The paper explicitly guards against evaluator leakage — the same VLM scores outputs AND gates memory writes — by using blind human judgement as the headline metric and VLM scores only as auxiliary diagnostics (§3, §4.3, p.6) — direct precedent for MF's fidelity concern about self-referential evaluation loops.

A Random-EMB (shuffled content, matched retrieval budget) baseline isolates format effects from actual memory content ('rules out generic memory-format-context explanations', Table 1) — a rigorous measured-retrieval control matching MF's G-M2 stance.

notes: Table 1 (p.8, headline + ablation blocks) is the load-bearing evidence; the explicit evaluator-leakage discussion (§3, p.6) is notable methodology. Not RECONSIDERAR — clearly on-topic dual-channel negative/positive memory paper.

cita: Talebirad et al. (2026). From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents.
problema: In multi-agent LLM coordination (here, inventing a shared communication code from scratch in a Lewis signaling game), it is unclear whether successful convention formation is driven mainly by channel/vocabulary capacity or by what kind of persistent memory architecture each agent carries across rounds, since prior work treats capacity as the main lever and rarely controls for memory structure.
mecanismo: Five memory architectures (stateless rolling-window-only, a shared environment-compiled convention board, a private overwritten free-text scratchpad, a private fixed-capacity slot-list codebook, and a codebook plus a persistent meta-note) are compared for two frozen LLM agents (sender/receiver) playing 200-round signaling games; each store differs only in how it is updated (overwrite, in-place slot edit, or environment-compiled), and three studies isolate memory architecture from channel capacity and from history-window length.
evaluacion: Study 1 compares all five architectures at fixed capacity (3 seeds); Study 2 sweeps channel capacity |V|^L from 4 to 125 for the two most distinct architectures (up to 8 seeds at the predicted bottleneck); Study 3 sweeps the rolling-window size directly to separate consolidation from raw history length; metrics are task accuracy, TopSim compositionality, positional mutual information, and lexicon collision rate.
numeros_clave: Persistent private scratchpad reaches 0.867+-0.023 accuracy at capacity=25, the most reliable coordination in the study, avoiding the high-capacity collapse of stateless 'memory only' agents (0.80->0.52 at cap=64, collision rate 1.0); the predicted information-bottleneck optimum (cap=8) is instead a fragility point (bimodal outcomes, permutation p=0.024); un-pruned codebook memory peaks early (P1-color purity 0.96 at 50 rounds) but degrades to 0.527+-0.13 late-game accuracy as stale/conflicting slots accumulate; codebook-plus-meta-note ends lowest (0.460+-0.14) because the meta-note freezes into generic restated instructions rather than higher-order insight (Study 1 discussion, Table 2-3, p.3-4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The un-pruned slot-list ('codebook') memory shows fast early convergence but no durable consolidation: without a pruning mechanism, stale and conflicting entries accumulate over 200 rounds and drag performance down to 0.527 late-game accuracy (Study 1 discussion, p.3-4) — a measured negative result supporting MF's stance that unbounded, unpruned memory accumulation degrades usefulness over time.

The 'codebook meta' condition adds a persistent meta-note meant to capture higher-order structural rules, but inspection shows the note freezes by round 30 into generic restatements of the prompt's own instructions rather than genuine distilled insight, making it the weakest private-memory condition (0.460+-0.14, p.4) — a cautionary data point about naive self-summarization as a consolidation mechanism, without directly confirming or refuting a specific MF choice.

The single shared public convention table ('env board') achieves the highest raw accuracy (0.827+-0.09) precisely because both agents read one authoritative source instead of maintaining separate private derived conventions, though at the cost of near-zero compositional structure (a memorized lookup, not a productive code, §Study 1) — supports MF's single-source-per-fact stance while flagging its tradeoff against agent-internal understanding.

notes: Table 2/3 (p.3-4, Study 1) and Table 4/5 + Fig.4 (Study 2, p.5) are the load-bearing numbers; domain is emergent-communication research (Lewis signaling games), not software agents, but the core finding (memory architecture > channel capacity; un-pruned memory degrades) is a direct, generalizable memory-architecture result. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Toeda (2026). Memory Is Not Live State — Cross-Agent Memory Governance by Transplanting the Reflective Context Governor onto Agent Memory (memgov v0.1.0).
problema: Persistent agent memory is written as a snapshot of the world but the world keeps changing after the snapshot is taken; in a workspace with two or more agents working in parallel sessions, status-bearing memory claims ('not yet deposited', 'tool X is broken') go stale routinely and are trusted at session start as if they were current truth, with no mechanism verifying them against the world before the agent acts.
mecanismo: A commitment-surface table (SHARED_STATE) holds one row per cross-agent live fact, each with an absolute date and a verification anchor (a command/path/API yielding ground truth); a deterministic drift scanner sweeps every fragmented memory store for lines that still assert a status the commitment surface says is resolved, producing a CONFLICT_MAP; flagged lines enter a non-compensatory review queue (no plausibility/recency can excuse a flagged claim, only verification against the anchor); a freshness heartbeat flags stale status-bearing files with governed friction (suppression after reconciliation) to avoid training users to ignore warnings; each agent corrects only its own store, with cross-agent fixes routed through the shared commitment surface.
evaluacion: A real two-agent (Claude Code + GPT Codex) workspace incident (2026-07-06/07) is analyzed for root cause, the countermeasure (memgov v0.1.0) is deployed the same day, and the first scan-repair-rescan cycle is measured via an append-only ledger; a companion RCGov (context-governance) engine comparison is planned but not yet run.
numeros_clave: First full scan: 73 memory files across 4 stores vs 7 committed rows -> 17 suspected drifts, including 3 papers misremembered as unpublished (already published the prior day) and a repaired toolchain still remembered as broken (12 days stale); after correction, re-scan -> 14 remaining drifts (§5); freshness heartbeat default threshold 2 days, suppression 3 days after reconciliation (§4); released tool is 124 KB with zero runtime dependencies and 10 tests (§6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central incident is a stale-memory near-miss: an agent's persistent memory asserted a status-bearing claim ('not yet deposited') that had been false for a day, caught only because a machine-readable ledger was consulted before acting (§2) — direct real-world evidence for MF's FIDELIDAD concern about staleness and provenance in memory.

SHARED_STATE is literally a plan/status table — one row per status-bearing fact with an absolute date and a verification anchor, overwritten in place by whichever session changes it (§4 point 1) — a concrete, deployed instance of plan-state-as-first-class-memory, directly matching MF's PLAN-ESTADO axis.

Root-cause analysis names three structural findings worse than the individual error — store fragmentation, an unsatisfiable guard that trained its audience to ignore it, and 12-day-stale cross-agent memory (§2) — the paper explicitly captures 'what went wrong structurally' as durable governance knowledge, not just the incident.

A drift scanner sweeps every fragmented private memory store against the single committed SHARED_STATE table and flags contradictions as a CONFLICT_MAP (§4 points 1-2) — a concrete single-source-of-truth-vs-multi-store reconciliation mechanism MF could adopt for its own multi-store seams.

notes: §2 incident timeline (2026-07-06/07) and §5 first-scan ledger figures (17->14 drifts) are the load-bearing evidence; the paper names an AI co-observer in its method note, which does not affect the measured incident/ledger claims. Not RECONSIDERAR — a first-party governance case study squarely on FIDELIDAD/PLAN-ESTADO.

cita: Xiong, Z., Lin, Y., Xie, W., He, P., Liu, Z., Tang, J., Lakkaraju, H., & Xiang, Z. (2025). How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior.
problema: Memory addition and deletion are core, widely-used operations in LLM agent episodic memory, but their long-term behavioral effects are poorly understood: naive strategies risk silently degrading agent performance over time as noisy or misaligned past experiences accumulate and get replayed as demonstrations.
mecanismo: Controlled experiments isolate memory addition (add-all vs. three automatic 'coarse' trajectory evaluators vs. a strict human/oracle evaluator vs. a fixed-memory no-addition baseline) and memory deletion (periodic frequency-based, history-based utility-weighted, and a combined strategy) across a synthetic RegAgent and three real agents (EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT Agent), measuring the correlation between input-similarity and output-similarity of retrieved demonstrations (the 'experience-following' property) and comparing against error-free ground-truth counterfactuals to isolate error propagation.
evaluacion: Long-running execution streams (thousands of tasks) across 4 agents, 5 addition evaluators and 3 deletion strategies, tracking success-rate/accuracy vs. memory size (Tables 1-2), plus stress tests under task-distribution shift and memory-capacity constraints.
numeros_clave: Strict evaluator: AgentDriver success rate 51.00 (mem size 1178) vs add-all 32.32 (mem 2125) vs fixed-memory baseline 40.11 (mem 180); CIC-IoT strict 85.40 vs add-all 59.90 (Table 1); combined deletion on CIC-IoT reaches 85.50 accuracy at mem size 188 (vs 904 with no deletion, Table 2); history-based deletion + strict evaluator on AgentDriver (51.81) exceeds the error-free ground-truth counterfactual (§4.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: 'Error propagation' is measured directly: noisy add-all/coarse-evaluator memories cause a persistent performance gap vs. an error-free ground-truth counterfactual that widens as execution continues (§3.4, Fig.4) — hard evidence that ungated writes actively poison future agent behavior, supporting MF's negative-knowledge / anti-poisoning stance.

Memory addition is explicitly gated by a trajectory evaluator (add-all vs. coarse-automatic vs. strict/human), and a fine-tuned coarse evaluator (300 examples) already rivals the strict human gate while beating add-all on every agent (Table 1, p.4) — concrete evidence for MF's write-trigger stance that admission must be judged, not automatic.

History-based deletion — removing records whose average downstream retrieval utility falls below a threshold — outperforms simple frequency-based pruning and, on AgentDriver, even beats the error-free baseline (§4.2-4.3, Table 2) — a measured recipe for promoting/demoting stored experience by outcome rather than recency.

The 'experience-following' property (near-perfect correlation between input and output similarity, Fig.3, §3.3) formalizes how directly agents imitate retrieved records — a measurable diagnostic MF could reuse to detect when its own memory is being copied verbatim rather than reasoned over.

notes: Table 1/2 (p.4/6) and Fig.3/4 (experience-following, error propagation) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a core empirical memory-management study, squarely on-topic.

cita: Xu (2025). Memory Management and Contextual Consistency for Long-Running Low-Code Agents.
problema: Long-running low-code/no-code (LCNC) agents suffer 'memory inflation' (dialogue/tool history growing linearly and blowing the context window and token cost) and 'contextual degradation' (older critical information being pushed out, causing incoherent, self-contradicting behavior), and non-technical LCNC users have no way to inspect or correct what the agent remembers.
mecanismo: A hybrid episodic+semantic memory store applies an 'Intelligent Decay' mechanism: each episodic entry gets a composite Utility Score S = alpha*Recency + beta*Relevance(cosine) + gamma*UserUtility; entries below a threshold are deleted or, if flagged, LLM-summarized into the semantic store (Algorithm 1); a proposed timeline UI lets non-technical users pin/forget/consolidate memories directly, setting the UserUtility term as a hard human-in-the-loop signal.
evaluacion: A single simulated long-running LCNC task (drafting a multi-week project plan over 500 turns) compares a 10-turn sliding-window baseline, a basic-RAG (episodic retrieval, no decay) baseline, and the proposed hybrid system on task completion rate, token cost, latency, and an LLM-judge consistency/contradiction-rate metric (Table 1, Fig.2).
numeros_clave: Table 1: task completion 65.2% (sliding window) / 81.4% (basic RAG) / 92.5% (hybrid); average token cost per turn 580/1150/890; contradiction rate 18.1%/5.5%/1.2%. However, Appendix A's own simulation code shows the headline Figure 2 'self-degradation vs. self-evolution' curves are produced by hand-written exponential-decay and hard-clamped functions explicitly commented 'for realistic visualization', not by measured agent runs — this digest cites Table 1 but flags it as unverified/simulated evidence (§5, Appendix A).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper frames its design around the 'self-degradation' problem measured in prior real work (error propagation / misaligned experience replay, cited as ref [6]), but its own demonstration of that problem (Fig.2 'All-Add' decay curve) is a hand-tuned simulation per Appendix A's code, not an independent measurement, so it should not be read as additional confirming evidence on its own.

Appendix A's simulation code (hardcoded exponential decay plus a range 'clamped ... for realistic visualization') reveals that the headline self-degradation-vs-evolution curve is synthetic rather than measured — a direct illustration of MF's FIDELIDAD concern (fabricated/unverifiable evidence) applied to the source paper itself, not just to agent memories it describes.

The Intelligent Decay Utility Score S=alpha*R+beta*E+gamma*U with a threshold-gated consolidate-or-delete branch (§3.2, Algorithm 1) is a concrete, tunable formalization of gotcha promotion/pruning MF could reference as a design pattern, independent of whether this paper's own evaluation is simulated.

A reported 22% token-cost reduction versus basic RAG alongside higher task completion (Table 1, §5.3) matches MF's context-economy framing, though the FIDELIDAD caveat above applies to how confidently this specific number should be trusted.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: Appendix A's own simulation code (hardcoded exponential-decay and hand-clamped ranges explicitly commented 'for realistic visualization') indicates Figure 2, and plausibly Table 1, are synthetic illustrations rather than measured agent runs; reference [6] also appears to attribute the real experience-following/self-degradation study (cf. the Xiong et al. paper in this same digestion wave) to different, seemingly fictitious authors and a mismatched venue (Nature Communications). Digested per protocol; flagging for human review given the evidence-fabrication risk.
